rounds.fact: Photobucket became the default way millions of MySpace users hosted images for their profiles, since MySpace itself didn't offer easy photo uploading in its early years.
Winamp's slogan 'It really whips the llama's ass' became one of the most recognizable taglines of the early MP3 era, and its skinnable interface inspired an entire community of custom designs.
StumbleUpon's whole concept was a browser button that took you to a random, algorithm-picked website matching your interests, a discovery model that faded as social feeds took over that role.
Tucows started in 1993 as a curated shareware download library (the name stood for 'The Ultimate Collection of Winsock Software') before evolving into an internet services company.
Tom's Hardware built its reputation on exhaustive PC component benchmarks, becoming one of the go-to sites for hardware enthusiasts well before mainstream tech blogs existed.
